mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows, and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a tightening cycle, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.5% in the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices over 60 days indicates a robust economic expansion, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 and INDPRO rising, or the proxies do not exhibit the required concurrent growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) and rise in employment (PAYEMS) over 20 days signals a strengthening labor market, enhancing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both PAYEMS decreasing and UNRATE decreasing, or the proxies do not show the expected simultaneous decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% triggers monetary tightening, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS rising above 4%, or the regime condition is not met.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, a sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index below 2% reduces inflationary pressures, lowering risk premiums and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite CPIAUCSL falling below 2%, or the inflation rate does not meet the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected surge in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% in a labor market tightening cycle signals weakening demand, reducing corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite UNRATE exceeding 5.5%, or the unemployment rate does not rise above the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in demand (GDPC1) and fall in unemployment (PAYEMS) over 5 days indicates a strong economic upturn, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 rising and PAYEMS falling, or the proxies do not exhibit the required concurrent movement.
